note: Owner-editable (2026-09-28: 'we need to automate every aspect before another playtest'). Features that are not fight mechanics, so the sheet does not list them as 'not automated yet': build (a choice made when the character is built; its result is already in the build), outside (used away from the table's fights: rituals, relationships, investigation, crafting, travel), definition (a rules definition other features use; nothing of its own to run), applied (the fight already does what it says, in the build or the table's own handling), table (needs something the table does not model yet: climbing, elevation, falling, mounts). Keys are typed-mechanic ids; 'why' is shown on the sheet. Anything not listed here and not automated stays in 'not automated yet'.

WRESTLING_BASE_RESTRAINTS_AND_UTILIZE.why: Combat equipment behaviour, not a non-combat reminder: when a Wrestling talent lets you secure a creature with Rope, Chains, Manacles or a similar restraint (Pin's window, Capture Specialist), securing it costs the Utilize Action - a Bonus Action with Capture Specialist - meets the item's own requirements, and keeps the item's own escape and break rules unless the talent replaces them. The table has no restraint-item rules to run that with: the equipment catalog's Rope, Chain and Manacles rows carry only name, weight and price, so there is no binding check, permitted-size limit, bound condition, escape DC or break DC to apply, and no item action tracks who is bound. Left to the GM until those item rules exist.

WRESTLING_BASE_GRAPPLING_REMINDER.why: The 2024 grapple rules the table's grapple follows.

EQUIPMENT_BASE_FITTED_ARMOR_DESIGNATION.why: The armour the character wears counts as its Fitted Armor.

TAL_ATHLETICS_WALL_STUNT.why: Run up or along walls as difficult ground: the climb route costs two feet of movement per foot, a creature at least two sizes larger counts as a wall once the GM approves it (and moving on it provokes that creature's Opportunity Attack), and ending your turn on a wall with nothing to hold makes you fall. The table's own climbing, movement cost, Opportunity Attack and falling rules run all of it.
